atoms.text: This guide describes how to give the Ridgeline Query service access to an S3 bucket named example-analytics-data. The service reads compressed clickstream files from the raw/clickstream/ prefix and writes query results to the results/ridgeline/ prefix of the same bucket. Queries run under an IAM role named RidgelineQueryRole in account 111122223333, which the service assumes at job start. Create an identity-based policy and attach it to RidgelineQueryRole. The policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-analytics-data/raw/clickstream/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-analytics-data/results/ridgeline/*. It also allows s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on arn:aws:s3:::example-analytics-data, with an s3:prefix condition that limits listing to those two prefixes. Do not modify the bucket policy; the bucket carries no statement for this role, and the grant exists only in the policy attached to the role. After attaching the policy, submit a test query and confirm that a result object appears under results/ridgeline/. If the query fails with AccessDenied, check the resource ARNs in the identity-based policy for typos in the bucket name or prefix.

This guide describes how to give the Ridgeline Query service access to an S3 bucket named example-analytics-data. The service reads compressed clickstream files from the raw/clickstream/ prefix and writes query results to the results/ridgeline/ prefix of the same bucket. Queries run under an IAM role named RidgelineQueryRole in account 111122223333, which the service assumes at job start. Add a statement to the bucket policy whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/RidgelineQueryRole. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-analytics-data/raw/clickstream/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-analytics-data/results/ridgeline/*. It also allows s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on arn:aws:s3:::example-analytics-data, with an s3:prefix condition that limits listing to those two prefixes. Do not attach any S3 permissions to the role itself; the role has no identity-based policy for this bucket, and the grant exists only in the bucket policy. After saving the policy, submit a test query and confirm that a result object appears under results/ridgeline/. If the query fails with AccessDenied, check the Principal ARN in the bucket policy for typos in the account ID or role name.

This guide covers access for a nightly Tessera Batch job that converts Parquet input into aggregated output files. The job runs from a scheduler host that authenticates as an IAM user named tessera-batch-runner, using an access key stored in the scheduler's secret file. The job reads from s3://example-warehouse-input/sales/daily/ and writes to s3://example-warehouse-output/sales/aggregates/. Create a customer managed policy and attach it to the IAM user tessera-batch-runner. The policy grants s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the input bucket, and s3:PutObject on the sales/aggregates/ prefix of the output bucket. Neither bucket policy is edited, so both buckets keep their existing policies and the grant is carried only by the user's attached policy. Limit the s3:ListBucket statement to the sales/daily/ prefix with an s3:prefix condition. Run the job manually once and verify that an output object is created with a current timestamp. If the run fails, confirm the access key is active and belongs to the intended user.

This guide covers access for a nightly Tessera Batch job that converts Parquet input into aggregated output files. The job runs from a scheduler host that authenticates as an IAM user named tessera-batch-runner, using an access key stored in the scheduler's secret file. The job reads from s3://example-warehouse-input/sales/daily/ and writes to s3://example-warehouse-output/sales/aggregates/. Add a statement to each bucket's policy, naming arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/tessera-batch-runner as the Principal. The statement on the input bucket grants s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket, and the statement on the output bucket grants s3:PutObject on the sales/aggregates/ prefix. The IAM user has no attached policy for these buckets, so the grant is carried only by the two bucket policies. Limit the s3:ListBucket statement to the sales/daily/ prefix with an s3:prefix condition. Run the job manually once and verify that an output object is created with a current timestamp. If the run fails, confirm the access key is active and the Principal ARN matches the intended user.

This guide explains how to let the Lumen Ad-hoc query service write result sets to a dedicated results bucket named example-query-results. The service only writes to this bucket; the source data it queries is held elsewhere and is not covered here. Jobs run with an IAM role named LumenQueryExecutionRole in account 111122223333. Attach an identity-based policy to that role that allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::example-query-results/output/*. Add s3:GetBucketLocation and s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::example-query-results to the same policy, because the service checks the bucket's location before writing. The bucket policy stays unchanged, and example-query-results has no statement referring to the role. Result files are written as CSV under output/ followed by the query ID. After a test query, list the output/ prefix and confirm that the CSV object exists and is non-empty. A 403 response on upload normally indicates that the resource ARN in the role's policy is missing the /* suffix.

This guide explains how to let the Lumen Ad-hoc query service write result sets to a dedicated results bucket named example-query-results. The service only writes to this bucket; the source data it queries is held elsewhere and is not covered here. Jobs run with an IAM role named LumenQueryExecutionRole in account 111122223333. Add a statement to the bucket policy with Principal set to the account ID 111122223333, which admits principals in that account, and allow s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::example-query-results/output/*. Add s3:GetBucketLocation and s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::example-query-results to the same policy, because the service checks the bucket's location before writing. The role carries no S3 permissions of its own, and the grant lives only in the bucket policy. Result files are written as CSV under output/ followed by the query ID. After a test query, list the output/ prefix and confirm that the CSV object exists and is non-empty. A 403 response on upload normally indicates that the Resource ARN in the bucket policy statement is missing the /* suffix.

This guide describes access for the Corvid Stream Aggregator, which ingests event files from a landing bucket and removes them after processing. The bucket is named example-event-landing, and files arrive under the inbound/ prefix as gzip-compressed JSON lines. The aggregator runs as an IAM role named CorvidAggregatorRole and writes its rolled-up metrics to a separate database, so it does not write back to the bucket. Attach an identity-based policy to CorvidAggregatorRole that allows s3:GetObject and s3:DeleteObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-event-landing/inbound/*. Include s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::example-event-landing with a prefix condition for inbound/. The bucket policy is left as it is, with no statement added for this role. Deletion occurs only after the aggregator confirms the rollup is committed, so failed batches remain in place for retry. To verify, place a small test file under inbound/ and confirm it disappears after the next aggregation cycle. If files are read but not deleted, check that s3:DeleteObject appears in the role's attached policy.

This guide covers permissions for the Halden Report Exporter, which writes large daily report files to a bucket named example-report-archive. Reports are several gigabytes each, so the exporter uses multipart uploads and writes them under reports/daily/YYYY/MM/. The exporter runs as an IAM role named HaldenExporterRole in account 111122223333. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket, with object actions scoped to arn:aws:s3:::example-report-archive/reports/daily/*. Do not edit the bucket policy; the role's attached policy is the only place the grant is defined. The exporter reads its source tables from an internal database, so no read access to the bucket is needed. Configure the exporter's upload part size at 64 MiB to match its default setting. Run the exporter for a single day's report and confirm the final object size matches the expected row count output. Incomplete multipart uploads that remain after a failure indicate the abort permission is missing from the role's policy.

This guide describes how to grant the Piquet Validator service access to a bucket named example-ingest-staging. The validator reads a manifest file and the CSV data files it lists from the incoming/ prefix. Records that fail schema checks are written as rejected-record files to the quarantine/ prefix in the same bucket. The validator runs as an IAM role named PiquetValidatorRole in account 111122223333. Attach an identity-based policy toPiquetValidatorRole granting s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-ingest-staging/incoming/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-ingest-staging/quarantine/*. The role must not be able to write to incoming/, which keeps the source files unmodified. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket itself, limited by prefix condition to incoming/ and quarantine/. No change is made to the bucket policy, and the role's attached policy holds the entire grant. Test with a manifest that contains one deliberately malformed row, then confirm a rejected-record file appears under quarantine/. An AccessDenied on the quarantine write usually means the PutObject resource ARN points to the wrong prefix.

This guide explains access for the Sable Feature Builder, a job that reads historical records from a versioned bucket named example-history-store. Because versioning is enabled, the job pins each run to a specific object version recorded in its run configuration. It reads objects under the snapshots/ prefix and writes the derived feature tables to the features/ prefix of the same bucket. The job authenticates as an IAM user named sable-feature-builder in account 111122223333. Attach an identity-based policy to that user that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::example-history-store/snapshots/*, and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-history-store/features/*. Add s3:ListBucket and s3:ListBucketVersions on the bucket ARN. The bucket policy is not touched, and the user's attached policy carries the whole grant. Start a run against a known version ID and verify that the feature table is written with the expected row count. If a pinned version cannot be read, check that s3:GetObjectVersion is present in the user's policy.

This guide covers access for the Mortise Compactor, which merges many small files into larger ones within a partitioned dataset. The dataset lives in a bucket named example-lake-curated under the tables/orders/ prefix, partitioned by date. For each partition, the compactor lists the small files, reads them, writes one merged file, and deletes the originals. It runs as an IAM role named MortiseCompactorRole in account 111122223333. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, and s3:DeleteObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-lake-curated/tables/orders/*. Include s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::example-lake-curated with a prefix condition for tables/orders/. Leave the bucket policy unchanged; the grant is defined solely in the role's attached policy. Configure the compactor to delete originals only after the merged file is written successfully. Run it on one partition and confirm that a single merged object remains and the small files are gone. If the delete step fails, review the role's policy for a missing s3:DeleteObject action.
